open_points.subject: Registry-context request decoding
open_points.text: “the guard's request has no field for Registry context; an import or request carrying its own status or project facts is refused at decoding” does not define which fields count as “project facts”; every project-scoped request legitimately carries project_id.
open_points.question: Which exact client-supplied fields constitute forbidden Registry context, and is the required project_id expressly excluded?
options: Only Registry-owned context fields such as status, display_name, address and customer_ref are forbidden; project_id remains allowed.
Every client-supplied project fact, including project_id, triggers decoding refusal.
Only a structured Registry-context object is forbidden; otherwise unknown project-related fields are ignored.
open_points.default_guess: Allow project_id, reject every client-supplied Registry-owned context field, and reject unknown fields rather than ignoring them.

witness.initial: An active producer has an active grant and submits a valid version-1 snapshot for an active Registry project.
events: The producer sends the required project_id and otherwise valid snapshot content.
The portal decodes the request before consulting Registry.
outcomes: project_id is treated as the target identity, decoding succeeds, Registry is consulted, and the import proceeds.
project_id is treated literally as a client-supplied project fact, so decoding refuses the request before Registry is called.
witness.observer: The producer sees either an import result or a decoding rejection.

open_points.subject: Representation of source-supplied dates
open_points.text: A28 says source-supplied “document_date” and “payment_date” are “the same instant, stored offset-naive UTC like every persisted timestamp”, while State 1 defines both as date values, not instants or datetimes.
open_points.question: Are document_date and payment_date preserved as calendar dates, or converted into offset-naive UTC datetimes; if converted, what time and timezone determine the instant?
options: Preserve them as date values and exempt them from A28's instant representation rule.
Convert each date to a UTC datetime using a specified time and timezone.
Change the models and public views to carry source-supplied datetimes instead of dates.
open_points.default_guess: Preserve document_date and payment_date as dates; apply offset-naive UTC representation only to datetime-valued source times.

witness.initial: No payment with payment_id P exists.
events: An operator registers P with payment_date 2026-10-25.
outcomes: The portal persists and returns the calendar date 2026-10-25 as M33 and PaymentView require.
The portal treats the supplied value as an instant and persists an offset-naive UTC datetime, requiring an unstated time and timezone and changing the stored/API representation.
witness.observer: The operator or an API consumer sees a date in one implementation and a datetime-derived value in the other.

open_points.subject: CLK-001 Required tests
open_points.text: CLK-001 distinguishes equal event timestamps from “an expiry it derives from a TTL” which must equal that instant plus its TTL, but its Required test asks that the operation's “written timestamps, other than audit occurred_at, are one instant” without excluding expiry fields. The item also does not say to test the source-supplied-time preservation clause.
open_points.question: Which timestamp fields must the equality assertion include, and what Required test demonstrates TTL-derived expiry and preservation of source-supplied times?
options: Compare only portal-owned event timestamps; separately assert expiry = operation instant + TTL and each source-supplied value is preserved.
Treat expiry as one of the timestamps that must equal the operation instant, contradicting the TTL clause.
Leave expiry and source-supplied-time clauses without a Required test.
open_points.default_guess: Limit equality to event timestamps and add explicit assertions for TTL-derived expiries and source-supplied values.

witness.initial: The clock returns N; the staff-session TTL is 12 hours.
events: A successful login creates a session with created_at N and expires_at N plus 12 hours.
The CLK-001 Required test compares the operation's written timestamps.
outcomes: The test compares only event timestamps and accepts the required expiry N plus 12 hours.
The test includes expires_at, requires it to equal N, and rejects the implementation that follows CLK-001's TTL rule.
witness.observer: The verification author sees the same conforming implementation pass or fail depending on the unstated field set.

open_points.subject: Single time-source and elapsed-clock rules
open_points.text: The new rules require that one clock source is “the only reader” of both host clocks and that the elapsed clock is read once per request, never stored or converted to an instant, but CLK-001 and its Required tests cover only wall-clock values written by multi-write operations.
open_points.question: Which formal invariant and Required test verify exclusive host-clock access, one elapsed-clock reading per request, monotonic duration use, and the prohibition on storing or converting elapsed readings?
options: Add a formal invariant and a check that instruments the time source and forbids direct host-clock calls and elapsed-value persistence.
Extend CLK-001 and its Required test to cover both wall and elapsed clock rules.
Leave these absolute rules without a verification obligation.
open_points.default_guess: Use a separate invariant and an instrumented check for source exclusivity and elapsed-clock usage.

witness.initial: A viewer-entry limiter is at the edge of its configured window, and an injected time source counts elapsed-clock reads.
events: A viewer submits one entry request.
The transport guard evaluates the rate-limit window.
outcomes: The guard obtains one elapsed value from the declared time source and makes the decision from that value.
The guard reads the source twice or calls time.monotonic directly; a boundary-crossing second value changes whether the request is admitted, while every described CLK-001 test still passes.
witness.observer: The viewer sees admission in one implementation and concealed rate-limit refusal in the other; an instrumented verification also sees different clock-call counts.
